name: Batroun
tagline: A small fishing town with a Phoenician sea wall, a stone old quarter, lemonade, wineries and the most relaxed beach scene on the Lebanese coast.
highlight: Sunset over the sea from the old harbour, with a glass of the town's famous lemonade or a bottle of local wine.
shortDescription: An easy-going coastal town 55 km north of Beirut, with Phoenician and Ottoman remains, a lively harbour, beaches, restaurants and vineyards in the hills behind.
metaDescription: A Batroun travel guide: the Phoenician wall, the old town and cathedral, beaches and beach clubs, seafood and lemonade, the wine region behind the town, and a one-day plan from Beirut.
nearestAirport: Beirut Rafic Hariri (BEY), about 1 hour by road
knownFor: The Phoenician wall, the old town, beaches, lemonade, wine
goodFor: Beaches, food, wine, nightlife, a slow coastal stop

image.alt: The harbour and old stone houses of Batroun on the Lebanese coast

intro: Batroun is a small town on a rocky headland about 55 km north of Beirut. It was a Phoenician port, known as Botrys, and it later became a Roman and Crusader town, and its old quarter is a tight cluster of stone houses, churches, mosques and shops around a small harbour. It is less historic than Byblos and less of a tourist site, and it has become in recent years one of the most fashionable places on the coast.

The best-known relic is the Phoenician sea wall, a line of rock about 225 metres long that stretches into the sea, shaped and reinforced by Phoenician builders to make a natural breakwater for the harbour. The town also has a 19th-century Greek Orthodox cathedral, a Maronite church, and a market where fishermen sell their catch. In the summer, its beaches, beach clubs, cafés and restaurants make it a favourite weekend spot for Beirutis.

Behind the coast, the hills are dotted with vineyards, and Batroun has become the centre of a small wine region. The town also has a reputation for its lemonade, made from local lemons and served in the old town. It is in the north, a part of the country that has generally been calm compared with the south and the Bekaa, but check your government's advice.

whyVisit.intro: Batroun combines sea, food and wine in a small and attractive setting, and is a good place to rest between sightseeing days.

points.title: The Phoenician wall
points.text: A natural rock breakwater reinforced by the Phoenicians, believed to be about 2,500 years old, which still shelters the harbour.

points.title: A walkable old town
points.text: Narrow lanes of stone houses, churches and workshops lead to the harbour and the sea.

points.title: Beaches and beach clubs
points.text: Small sandy beaches and rocky bays with clubs offer swimming and sunset drinks from May to October.

points.title: Food and lemonade
points.text: Seafood restaurants, bakeries and the famous Batroun lemonade make it a good place to eat.

points.title: Wine and hills
points.text: Wineries in the hills behind the town welcome visitors for tastings and lunches.

attractionsIntro: The old town, the wall and the harbour can be seen in a couple of hours, and the beaches and wineries fill the rest of a day.

attractions.name: The Phoenician Wall

image.alt: The Phoenician sea wall at Batroun stretching into the Mediterranean

attractions.text: A rocky sea wall of about 225 metres, part natural and part shaped by Phoenician builders, which formed a harbour and a defence. It is best seen from the shore near the old port.
attractions.tip: Walk along the rocks at sunset.

attractions.name: The old town and the souk
attractions.text: A network of narrow lanes, restored stone houses, small shops and cafés around the harbour. It is pleasant to wander in the morning or evening.
attractions.tip: Try the lemonade at a café.

attractions.name: The Cathedral of St Stephen
attractions.text: A 19th-century Maronite cathedral in the old town, with a dome and a bell tower, and a Greek Orthodox church nearby.

attractions.name: The Roman theatre and rock-cut remains
attractions.text: The remains of a small Roman theatre carved out of the rock, and ancient rock-cut tombs on the outskirts.

attractions.name: The harbour and fish market
attractions.text: A small port with fishing boats, a fish market and restaurants with tables at the water's edge.

attractions.name: Beaches and beach clubs
attractions.text: Small sandy beaches and clubs along the coast, some public and some private.
attractions.tip: Check entry fees and dress codes.

thingsToDoIntro: Batroun is a place for slow days, sunsets and long lunches.

thingsToDo.title: Watch the sunset at the wall
thingsToDo.text: The sun sets over the sea behind the Phoenician wall and the harbour.
thingsToDo.tip: Bring a drink and a jacket.

thingsToDo.title: Drink lemonade in the old town
thingsToDo.text: Batroun's lemonade, sometimes mixed with orange blossom water, is a local speciality.

thingsToDo.title: Visit a winery
thingsToDo.text: Vineyards in the hills produce good wines, and several offer tastings and meals.
thingsToDo.tip: Book ahead and hire a driver.

thingsToDo.title: Spend a day at a beach
thingsToDo.text: Swim, sunbathe and have lunch at a beach club.
thingsToDo.tip: Go on a weekday to avoid crowds.

thingsToDo.title: Eat fresh seafood
thingsToDo.text: Restaurants serve fish, calamari and prawns.
thingsToDo.tip: Choose your fish at the counter.

thingsToDo.title: Go out in the evening
thingsToDo.text: Bars and restaurants stay busy until late in summer.

foodIntro: Batroun is a good place to eat well, with seafood, mezze and local produce.

foods.name: Batroun lemonade
foods.text: Fresh lemon juice with sugar, mint or orange blossom water, served over ice.

foods.name: Grilled fish
foods.text: Sea bream, sea bass and red mullet, grilled and served whole.

foods.name: Mezze
foods.text: Hummus, tabbouleh and other starters, served with local wine or arak.

foods.name: Local wine
foods.text: Wines from vineyards in the hills, including whites and rosés.

foods.name: Bread and manakish
foods.text: Freshly baked flatbread with za'atar or cheese.

accommodation.intro: Batroun has a growing number of boutique hotels and guesthouses, particularly in the old town and along the coast.

areas.name: The old town
areas.text: Small guesthouses and boutique hotels in stone houses, close to the harbour.

areas.name: The coast
areas.text: Beach resorts and hotels north and south of the town.

gettingThere.intro: Batroun is about 55 km north of Beirut on the coastal highway, about 20 minutes beyond Byblos.

options.text: About an hour from Beirut without traffic, and longer at the weekend.
options.detail: Avoid leaving Beirut on Friday evening or returning on Sunday evening.

options.text: Buses and shared taxis run from Beirut to Batroun.
Some tours combine Batroun with Byblos and Jeita.

gettingAround.intro: The old town is walkable, and a car or taxi helps to reach the beaches and wineries.

options.text: The old town, the harbour and the wall are within 10 minutes' walk.
Taxis take you to the beaches and wineries.

bestTime.headline: May–October
bestTime.summary: Batroun has a Mediterranean climate, and the beach season runs from May to October. Spring and autumn are the most comfortable.

seasons.text: Warm and green, with the sea still cool.
Hot and humid, and the busiest and most expensive season.
Warm sea, fewer people, and the grape harvest.
Mild and wet, with many places closed.

bestTime.avoid: August weekends, when the town is packed.

itinerary.title: One day in Batroun
itinerary.intro: The old town and wall in the morning, lunch and the beach, a winery in the late afternoon.

days.title: Sea, sun and wine
days.morning: The old town and the Phoenician wall.
days.afternoon: A seafood lunch and a swim.
days.evening: A winery tasting and sunset in town.

tipsIntro: Batroun is relaxed, and a few tips help.
tips: Go on a weekday in summer. The weekend crowd from Beirut can be heavy.
Book restaurants and beach clubs in advance in July and August.
Bring cash in US dollars, and check card fees.
Do not drink and drive. Use a driver for the wineries.
Check the current situation. Batroun has generally been calm, but conditions in Lebanon can change.
Dress modestly in the old town and churches.
Bring a jacket for the evening.

faq.a: Its Phoenician sea wall, its lemonade, its old town, its beaches and its growing wine scene.

faq.q: How long do you need in Batroun?
faq.a: One day is enough for the town, a swim and a winery. A night lets you enjoy the evening.
It is in the north, which has generally been calm compared with the south and the Bekaa, but conditions in Lebanon can change. Check your government's advice.

faq.q: How far is Batroun from Beirut?
faq.a: About 55 km, or an hour without traffic.
From May to October, with the water at its warmest in August and September.

faq.q: Can I combine Batroun with Byblos?
faq.a: Yes. They are about 20 minutes apart, and are often visited together.
